pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Upgrades J M Mhatre Infra to ‘IND BBB-’/Stable; Limits Enhanced
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has upgraded J M Mhatre Infra Pvt Ltd’s (JMMIPL) Long-Term Issuer Rating to ‘IND BBB-’ from ‘IND BB+’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are given below:
keyRatingDrivers:
Healthy Credit Metrics: The upgrade reflects a sustained improvement in JMMIPL’s EBITDA interest coverage (EBITDA/gross interest expense) which surpassed Ind-Ra’s expectations of 3.5x in FY17. As per FY17 provisional financials, EBITDA interest cover improved to 4.60x (FY16: 4.29x) and FFO interest coverage (FFO/gross interest) to 4.46x (2.56x) on account of an improvement in absolute EBITDA. In FY17P, EBITDA improved to INR1,012 million (FY16: INR990 million) including share of profit from joint ventures of INR217 million in (INR246 million) attributed to lower operating costs. EBITDA margins excluding share of profit in joint ventures was around 19% in FY17P (FY16: 18%). Gross leverage (total adjusted debt/operating EBITDAR) remained healthy, but deteriorated to 1.61x in FY17 (FY16: 1.33x) owing to an increase in fund-based borrowings for working capital purposes.

 

Ind-Ra expects the credit metrics to remain healthy in the medium term, despite an annual capex requirement of INR250 million for equipment infrastructure during FY18-FY20.

 

Strong Order Book: As of July 2017, JMMIPL had an order book of INR21.76 billion (4.9x of FY17 revenue of INR4,436 million), providing medium-term revenue visibility which is commensurate for the rating category. Ind-Ra expects JMMIPL to maintain revenue/order book multiple at around similar levels during FY18-FY20.

 

Non-Fund-Based Limits Enhanced: A fast growing order book translates into increased working capital requirements. JMMIPL has been sanctioned with additional non-fund-based facilities of INR450 million in January 2017, of which INR450 million remained unutilised as of July 2017. Ind-Ra believes this will facilitate JMMIPL to access higher mobilisation advances which in turn are likely to improve the liquidity position.

 

Working Capital Intensity: The company’s debtors account about 30% of its total revenue. JMMIPL’s utilisation of fund-based working capital limits was 94%-95% during the 12 months ended May 2017. Cash flow from operations declined to INR599 million in FY17P (FY16: INR914 million), although remained positive. The decline was on account of an increase in debtor collection period to 172 days in FY17 (FY16: 131 days).

Concentration and Competition Risk: The ratings are constrained by the company’s concentrated order book as it derives a majority of its orders from the roads sector. It also faces intense competition from companies in the infrastructure industry, particularly in the roads sector.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: A substantial increase in the scale of operations, diversification of order book and successful demonstration of execution of complex infrastructure projects while sustaining the credit metrics would be positive for the ratings.

 

Negative: A substantial decline in the scale of operations, a stretch in the liquidity position driven by deterioration in the working capital cycle, a fall in interest coverage below 3x could lead to a rating downgrade.
companyProfile:
JMMIPL began operations in 1985 as a partnership firm and was converted to a private limited company in 2010. It is engaged in the construction of roads, water supply systems, storm water management systems, sewage works, railway over bridges, among others. It is registered as an AA Class contractor with Maharashtra State Public Works Department.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market. 

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance and leasing companies, managed funds, urban local bodies and project finance companies. 

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Reserve Bank of India and National Housing Bank. 

India Ratings is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.

For more information, visit www.indiaratings.co.in.
